Declared that the Copyright Amendment Bill 2025, Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 2) Bill 2025 and Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework Bill) 2025 stand referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Argued that the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Bill 2025 provides overdue legal clarity for digital tokens and platforms but is insufficient to address stablecoins, debanking, tokenisation, licensing flexibility and Australia's loss of investment, jobs and capability; urged faster action and a broader strategy.

Supported the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Bill 2025, arguing that digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms should meet comparable licensing, custody, segregation, reconciliation, disclosure and oversight standards, with an 18-month adjustment window to protect consumers while supporting innovation.

Presented and moved adoption of the Selection of Bills Committee report, recommending referrals of bills on digital assets, veterans services, higher education and superannuation. Amendments concerning gambling advertising, telecommunications and coal mining long service leave were debated, with the amended motion ultimately agreed to.

Tabled an addendum and correction to the explanatory memorandum for the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Bill 2025 and moved amendments providing for an independent review and written reasons when an AustralianADI refuses financial services; the bill was read a third time.
